claims.text: FeNiCrMn produced by conventional one-step casting has a relatively coarse microstructure.
Conventionally cast FeNiCrMn may exhibit elemental segregation.
FeNiCrMn can be prepared by arc melting with at least eight remelting cycles followed by drop casting into a water-cooled mold.
The arc-melting and remelting process can be conducted under a high-purity argon atmosphere.
Room-temperature tensile testing can be used for mechanical evaluation of the processed alloy.
Repeated remelting followed by water-cooled drop casting will reduce the grain size of FeNiCrMn.
Repeated remelting followed by water-cooled drop casting will make the elemental distribution in FeNiCrMn more uniform.
Repeated remelting promotes complete mixing of the constituent elements.
Repeated remelting minimizes elemental segregation in FeNiCrMn.
Repeated remelting leads to grain refinement in FeNiCrMn.
The refined and more homogeneous microstructure enhances solid-solution strengthening.
The microstructural improvement favorably modifies dislocation motion.
The proposed processing route will increase the yield strength of FeNiCrMn relative to conventional one-step casting.
The proposed processing route will improve the ductility of FeNiCrMn relative to conventional one-step casting.
The yield-strength and ductility improvements will be statistically significant.
Conventionally cast FeNiCrMn has lower mechanical performance than FeNiCrMn produced by the proposed route.
The hypothesis is limited to FeNiCrMn processed under the specified conditions and is not assumed to generalize to other compositions or processing methods.
The magnitude of any mechanical-property improvement is uncertain and may depend on diffusivity, segregation tendencies, and further process optimization.
